extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, applicants, counsel, administrative patent judges, and USPTO Board staff
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, definitions, standards, and procedural requirements governing interferences, contested cases, and related Board practice under 37 CFR Part 41 (e.g., claim correspondence, priority motions, ex parte communications, extensions, expungement, appeals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'involved claim'
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on a similar definition in Rule 601(f) and consistent with the definition of 'involved' for contested cases in § 41.100: only claims that correspond to the count are at risk in an interference, except to the extent a question is raised as to whether a claim that does not correspond should.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only claims corresponding to the count are considered 'involved'; if a question arises whether a non-corresponding claim should be involved, that question must be raised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'senior party'
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'senior party' determination focuses on the earliest constructive reduction to practice to determine which party, if any, is senior (a departure from the current Rule 601(m)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority is determined by earliest constructive reduction to practice rather than prior formulation in Rule 601(m).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'threshold issue'
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrase 'threshold issue' includes three specific issues that directly affect whether a party may participate in an interference: (1) no interference-in-fact, (2) the bar under 35 U.S.C. 135(b), and (3) lack of written description under 35 U.S.C. 112(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 135(b) and 112(1) issues are directed to prevention of spuriously provoked interferences and are limited to motions from a party with a patent or published application against a party with an involved application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant provocation requirements (§41.202(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: §41.202(a) restates the requirements of Rules 604, 607, and 608 for applicants provoking an interference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §41.202(a)(5) continues practice of looking at the applicant’s specification to determine the meaning of a copied claim (not the specification from which the claim was copied).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to add or copy claims to provoke an interference (§41.202(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: §41.202(c) restates the practice under Rule 605 of requiring an applicant to add a claim to provoke an interference, and adds requirements for applicants copying claims from patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant ordinarily must add a claim (or follow the rule's specific copying requirements) to properly provoke an interference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary proceeding standards for priority (§41.202(d)–(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: §41.202(d) sets forth the basis for a summary proceeding when an applicant does not appear able to show it would prevail on priority; §41.202(e) requires the showing must by itself, if unrebutted, warrant a determination of priority favorable to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restates Rule 608 and Rule 617 practice; eliminates the distinction between 608(a) and 608(b). A movant must make a sufficient unrebutted showing to merit summary disposition on priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for declaring an interference (§41.203)
rubrics_metrics.description: §41.203(a) states the standard for declaring a patent interference: the Director uses a two-way unpatentability test to determine whether claimed inventions interfere. §41.203(b) authorizes an administrative patent judge to declare the interference; §41.203(c) permits redeclaration sua sponte or in response to motions; §41.203(d) permits parties to suggest declaration/redeclaration to accommodate files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declaration is governed by a two-way unpatentability test and administrative patent judges have authority to declare or redeclare interferences, including on party suggestion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices of requested relief and priority statements (§41.204)
rubrics_metrics.description: §41.204 defines notices of requested relief in interferences: (a) simplifies formal requirements of the preliminary statement (renamed 'priority statement'); (b) codifies requirement for a list of motions and ordinarily limits a party to substantive motions consistent with its notice of requested relief; (c) sets no default times for statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should align substantive motions with their notice of requested relief; formal requirements simplified but parties remain limited to the relief they put forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement filings and termination standards (§41.205)
rubrics_metrics.description: §41.205 restates practice for filing settlement agreements (Rule 666) and implements 35 U.S.C. 135(c); §41.205(a) incorporates Rule 661 and provides that after a final decision, an interference is terminated when no appeal or other review has or can be taken — or when such appeal/review itself is terminated (e.g., issuance of mandate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interference termination rules tie to appeal/review timelines; parties must file settlement agreements per rule and understand when interference is considered terminated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common ownership and control of multiple parties (§41.206)
rubrics_metrics.description: §41.206 revises practice regarding commonly owned patents and applications in an interference to address cases involving a real party-in-interest with the ability to control the conduct of more than one party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules account for real-party control across multiple parties to avoid improper coordination or manipulation of proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption and evidentiary standards for priority (§41.207(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: §41.207(a)(1) recodifies the presumption regarding order of invention from Rule 657(a); §41.207(a)(2) recodifies evidentiary standards for proving priority from Rule 657(b) and (c), restating the standard in terms of the date of the earliest constructive reduction to practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority proof standards now framed around earliest constructive reduction to practice; evidentiary presumptions from prior rules carried forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim correspondence and its effect (§41.207(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: §41.207(b) clarifies claim correspondence practice and explicitly states effect: (1) patentability must be determined for claims, not counts; (2) a claim corresponds to the count if the subject matter of the claim would have been anticipated by or obvious (alone or in combination with prior art) in view of the subject matter of the count.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment of correspondence is based on anticipation/obviousness comparison of claim subject matter against the count's subject matter; patentability determinations remain claim-focused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption about prior art cited against an opponent (§41.207(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: §41.207(c) restates the presumption in Rule 637(a) that prior art cited against an opponent is presumed to apply against the movant’s claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior art used by one side is ordinarily deemed to apply against the other side's claims unless rebutted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus of substantive motions on priority (§41.208(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: §41.208(a) focuses substantive motions on the core questions of priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motions should be directed primarily at priority issues rather than peripheral matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof for movants (§41.208(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: §41.208(b) places the burden of proof on the movant and provides guidance on how to satisfy the burden of going forward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Movant must carry the burden to make a prima facie showing; guidance indicates what evidence or showing is required to shift burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirement for added/amended claims and counts (§41.208(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: §41.208(c)(1) requires a movant seeking to add or amend a claim to show that the added or amended claim is patentable. §41.208(c)(2) similarly requires a movant seeking to add or amend a count to show that the count does not include unpatentable subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any requested additions/amendments must be justified as patentable (claims) or as not encompassing unpatentable subject matter (counts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-references and placement of rules (e.g., §1.191, §1.959, §41.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain rules and addresses (e.g., interference correspondence address) were moved to Part 41 with cross-references from Part 1 (e.g., §1.1, §1.17) to reduce confusion and centralize Board-related rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should consult Part 41 for Board-specific requirements and use cross-references in Part 1 where provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing papers with the Board and permitted methods (§41.106)
rubrics_metrics.description: §41.106 provides directions on filing papers with the Board in contested cases, including interferences, and supersedes prior prohibitions (e.g., bans on facsimiles and certificates of mailing redirected to §41.106).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow §41.106 for acceptable filing methods and formats for contested cases; prior Part 1 prohibitions were adjusted to point to this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for extensions of time before the Board (§41.4 good cause)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §41.4(a) maintains a 'good cause' standard for extensions of time decided by the Board (distinguished from the 'sufficient cause' standard of §1.136(b) decided outside the Board). To establish good cause a party must show the delay was excusable under the circumstances and that the appellant exercised due diligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors include length of delay, knowledge of the time limit, circumstances beyond control, the party's negligence, and any unavoidable harm preventing timely filing (Zamot v. MSPB cited). Good cause is adjudicated by the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stipulated changes vs. extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: An authorized, stipulated change in a deadline is not an extension of the deadline and the rule should not be read as permitting the standard itself to be changed by Board order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not conflate stipulated deadline changes with formal extension requests; adding 'or Order of the Board' to the rule could create misapprehension and was not adopted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of late filings and revival (§41.4(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised §41.4(b) reflects that a late filing that results in an application becoming abandoned or a reexamination terminated will be excused if the application or proceeding is revived under §1.137. A late filing not resulting in abandonment/termination will be excused upon showing of excusable neglect or a Board determination that consideration on the merits is in the interest of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different remedies apply depending on whether abandonment/termination occurs; revival under §1.137 applies in certain cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disqualification proceedings before the Board (§41.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: §41.5 provides for disqualification proceedings before the Board (distinct from suspension/exclusion under Part 10), typically arising from conflicts of interest in contested cases; checks include certification by the Chief APJ and availability of judicial review under 35 U.S.C. 32.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disqualification is case-specific, may be mooted by counsel withdrawal, and is subject to oversight and review to protect due process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board approval for counsel withdrawal (§41.5(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: §41.5(c) requires Board approval to withdraw as counsel in a Board proceeding; approval should come from the part of the agency with jurisdiction over the application or patent at the time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement should not create practical difference for counsel (approval already required); withdrawal procedures follow the jurisdictional authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expungement of unauthorized papers (§41.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: §41.7(a) permits the Board to expunge unauthorized papers filed as part of a proceeding before the Board or while the Board has jurisdiction, and will not be used to prune applications arbitrarily; expungement triggers include violation of a rule or Board order and should be exceptional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should assume the Board does not want duplicate papers absent specific request; remedies for expungement include seeking entry of evidence in district court (35 U.S.C. 145/146) or petitioning the Board to challenge the expungement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on refiling previously filed papers (§41.7(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: §41.7(b) provides that a party may not file a paper previously filed in the same Board proceeding (even as an exhibit or appendix) without Board authorization or as provided by rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This avoids duplicate filings within the same proceeding and prevents using filings merely to place papers in the record without Board authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt reporting of changes in real party-in-interest and related cases (§41.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: §41.8 requires prompt reporting (within 20 days) of changes in the real party-in-interest or in related cases; the scope is similar to Fed. Cir. R. 47.5. Reporting aids scheduling, panel assignment, and ensures the Board is aware of related judicial/administrative events that may affect outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting obligations are not onerous for parties with effective docketing; failure to disclose related cases may implicate duty of candor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bar on ex parte communications with the Board (§41.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: §41.11 bars all ex parte communications about a pending case with any administrative patent judge and with any Board employee 'assigned to the proceeding'; non-merits ex parte communications may take place with other Board employees not assigned to the case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prohibition is intentionally strict to prevent abuse; clarifies that support staff typically are not assigned and informal contacts with non-assigned staff are not prohibited. Examples in the supplementary information are not exceptions to the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted informational communications and waiver nuances (ex parte examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Informing the Board in one proceeding of a related proceeding is not an ex parte communication about the contested case so long as the information does not extend beyond identifying information; citing a pending case for a general proposition is allowed if it does not discuss merits of the cited case; declining to participate constitutes a waiver of protections under the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should avoid merits-related informal discussions; one-sided communications are treated cautiously (transcripts may be required).

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation practice and reliance on primary authority (§41.12 / §41.106(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Relocated citation requirements (e.g., parallel citation to West and USPQ for contested cases) and guidance that discourages citation of non-binding secondary authority (e.g., MPEP); primary authority is preferred for legal issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board uses USPQ for patent practice relevance and includes West as a courtesy to courts; parties should cite primary authority when available and follow Board citation format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location of fees for Board practice (§41.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: §41.20 moves fees relevant to Board practice into Part 41 to co-locate fees with the rules that require them; cross-references (e.g., §1.17(b)) added for guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay attention to Part 41 for fee schedules pertaining to Board proceedings; some fees must be paid before jurisdiction passes to the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and prerequisites for appeals to the Board (§41.31)
rubrics_metrics.description: §41.31(a)(1)–(3) incorporate former §1.191(a) requirements: an appeal (e.g., after claims twice rejected or finally rejected) must be filed within the time period provided under §1.134; if an amendment is filed within §1.134, the applicant may not file an appeal outside the §1.134 time period and must wait for a new rejection before appealing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals are more restrictive than 35 U.S.C. 134 regarding timing; applicants must carefully track §1.134 deadlines and consequences of filing amendments.
